title: Left tackle Taylor Decker announces he’s returning to Lions for 2026 season
content:
INDIANAPOLIS — On Tuesday, Lions GM Brad Holmes and coach Dan Campbell said they would give left tackle Taylor Decker space as he weighed retirement this offseason. The hope was that Decker would give them an answer by the start of the new league year.

He didn’t make them wait much longer. Decker announced his return for the 2026 season on Instagram on Tuesday.

“Whom shall I send, and who will go for us,” Decker posted. “Here I am; SEND ME! #Year11.”

This is huge news for the Lions, as they work to reconfigure their offensive line. Losing Decker would’ve been a blow to those efforts. He’s the longest-tenured player on the roster and a reliable left tackle. Good tackles are hard to find. The Lions don’t need to look for a starter this season.

Decker spent the 2025 season nursing a nagging shoulder injury that will likely need daily maintenance and load management during the season if he wants to keep playing.

“I’ve left him alone,” Campbell said of Decker. “We had a conversation right when the season ended about him taking his time to figure out what he really feels like he wants to do (and) can do. I’ve left him alone there. I don’t want to say we haven’t had a conversation, but I’m leaving that between us. But there’ll be some. Look, if it’s not (Decker returning), then we’ve got to find a guy. But if it is, we’re still going to find a guy. Because as much as I love Deck, he’s got some things that are going to need some management. That’s kind of where we’re at. One way or another, we’re going to need somebody that can play over there and that can help us if we need them in a crunch or we need them as a starter.”

Another oft-mentioned player from Tuesday’s interview sessions is running back David Montgomery. Montgomery saw his touches decline this past season, as Jahmyr Gibbs took on the lead-back role in his third season. Montgomery signed a two-year extension during the 2024 season — halfway through Year 2 of the initial three-year contract he signed in 2023 — and at the time, it signaled a commitment to a player the Lions have said all the right things about. But Montgomery’s usage declined to a point where those involved are figuring out their next steps.

Holmes and Campbell seemed to imply that the ball is in Montgomery’s court.

“I’ve been in touch with David’s agent and his representation,” Holmes said Tuesday. “Obviously, look, we love David. He’s a great player. We would love to have him. Kind of want to put last year in the rearview and just move forward. But a player has to want to be at a certain place as well, so those conversations are still fluid and we’re just kind of seeing how it goes.”

“We talked at the very end of the year,” Campbell said. “… I like to give these guys their space and just let them kind of unwind a little bit in their own way. They don’t need me in their ear. But, certainly, he knows how I feel. Drew (Petzing) loves him — I mean, who wouldn’t? This guy is a heck of a back. We’ll just see where everything is at. Certainly, there have been healthy conversations. I’m sure Brad told you guys, probably mentioned that. All good, man. David’s a pro. We’ll figure this out.”

The Lions should have clarity on Montgomery over the next three weeks, with the new league year beginning March 11.
